title: ARYA GIRI versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2026:UHC:4169
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No.614 of 2026
Arya Giri . .....Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ......Respondent
Presence: Mr. Narendra Bali, learned counsel for the Applicant.
 Mr. Dinesh Chauhan, learned AGA for the State.
Hon'ble Ashish Naithani, J (Oral)
The present first bail application has been moved by the applicant
seeking his release on bail in connection with FIR/Case Crime No.764
of 2025, under Sections 103(1) and 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023, Police Station KotwaliJwalapur, District Haridwar.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has
been falsely implicated and the entire State's case rests upon
circumstantial evidence.
3. It is argued that the State's case is primarily based on the "last
seen" theory alleging that the deceased was last seen with the applicant
on 24.12.2025, whereas as per the postmortem report, the probable time
of death is around 29/30.12.2025, thereby creating a substantial and
unexplained gap which weakens the last seen circumstance. It is further
submitted that the cause of death has not been conclusively ascertained
and the viscera report is still awaited.
4. Learned counsel submits that the deceased was habitual of
consuming narcotic substances and even the postmortem doctor noticed
1
First Bail Application No.614 of 2026 --Arya Giri Vs. State of Uttarakhand
Ashish Naithani J.

multiple pinhole marks on the body of the deceased. It is also argued
that the alleged recovery of injections, syringes and empty vial has
been falsely planted and no independent witness has been associated
with the recovery proceedings.
5. It is further submitted that the investigation stands completed,
charge-sheet has already been filed, the applicant has no criminal
history and is in custody since 02.01.2026. Therefore, prayer has been
made to enlarge the applicant on bail.
6. Per contra, learned State Counsel opposed the bail application
and submitted that the applicant is specifically named in the FIR and
the State's case clearly establishes that the deceased was last seen in the
company of the applicant.
7. It is submitted that during investigation, recovery of injections,
syringes and empty vial of Avil has been effected at the instance of the
applicant and the State's case further reveals that the deceased died due
to overdose intentionally administered by the applicant.
8. It is also argued that the offence alleged is grave in nature and in
case the applicant is enlarged on bail, there remains possibility of
influencing witnesses or misuse of liberty.
9. This Court has considered the rival submissions advanced by
learned counsel for the parties and perused the material brought on
record.
10. At this stage, it is not in dispute that the present case is entirely
based upon circumstantial evidence. The principal circumstance relied
upon by the State is that the deceased was allegedly last seen with the
applicant on 24.12.2025. However, from perusal of the postmortem
2
First Bail Application No.614 of 2026 --Arya Giri Vs. State of Uttarakhand
Ashish Naithani J.

report, it appears that the probable time of death has been opined to be
around 24 to 36 hours prior to the postmortem conducted on
31.12.2025, thereby prima facie indicating that the death likely
occurred around 29/30.12.2025. Thus, there appears to be a substantial
gap between the alleged last seen circumstance and the probable time
of death. At this stage, the necessary proximity required to firmly
establish the last seen theory does not appear to be prima facie
established.
11. Further, the post mortem report admittedly does not conclusively
ascertain the cause of death and the viscera report is still awaited. Thus,
at this stage, there is no definite medical opinion conclusively
establishing homicidal death. Though the State alleges that overdose of
narcotic substance was intentionally administered by the applicant, the
same would remain subject to evidence during trial and at present the
medical evidence has not attained conclusiveness.
12. So far as the alleged recovery is concerned, the same was
effected subsequently after recovery of the dead body and no
independent public witness appears to have been associated in the
recovery proceedings. The evidentiary value and admissibility of such
recovery would be matters to be adjudicated during trial.
13. The investigation already stands completed and charge-sheet has
been filed before the competent court. Thus, no further custodial
interrogation of the applicant appears necessary. The applicant is in
judicial custody since 02.01.2026.
14. The learned court below, while rejecting the bail application,
mainly proceeded on the seriousness of accusation and the recovery
3
First Bail Application No.614 of 2026 --Arya Giri Vs. State of Uttarakhand
Ashish Naithani J.

allegedly effected at the instance of the applicant. However, the aspects
relating to uncertainty regarding exact cause of death, incompleteness
of medical evidence and the substantial time gap in the last seen
circumstance do not appear to have been sufficiently considered at that
stage.
15. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and
considering the nature of accusations, evidence available on record,
period of incarceration, completion of investigation and the settled
principles governing grant of bail, this Court is of the opinion that the
applicant has made out a fit case for grant of bail.
ORDER
16. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
17. Let the applicant Arya Giri be released on bail in connection with
FIR/Case Crime No.764 of 2025, under Sections 103(1) and 238 BNS,
Police Station Kotwali Jwalapur, District Haridwar, on his furnishing a
personal bond and two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the
satisfaction of the court concerned.
 (Ashish Naithani, J.)
22.05.2026
